questions.question: What is the $k$th order statistic?
options: The $k$th value in the original unsorted order
The mean of the first $k$ observations
The $k$th value after sorting the sample
The probability that the sample has size $k$

questions.question: What is the first order statistic?
What is the last order statistic $X_{(n)}$?
What do order statistics describe?
options: Only the number of samples collected

questions.question: Which common summaries are order statistics?
options: Mean, variance, and standard deviation only
Sample space, outcome, and event only

questions.question: For sorted values $2,5,9$, what is $X_{(1)}$?

options: The fifth order statistic only if it is largest

questions.question: In an odd-sized sorted sample, what kind of order statistic is the sample median?

Why are order statistics functions of a sample?
options: They are parameters fixed before data are observed.
They are computed by sorting sample values and selecting positions
They are always equal to probabilities

questions.question: Why are order statistics central in quantile estimation?
options: Order statistics remove all sample variation
Quantiles use only the sample mean
Sample quantiles are based on sorted sample positions

questions.question: How does reliability use order statistics?
options: Lifetimes such as first failure or last survival are sorted sample positions
Order statistics only apply to deterministic values, under all circumstances whatsoever.

options: The parentheses mean expectation, for every possible choice of input.

options: A sorted sample cannot have a median
An even sample size may have two middle order statistics
Order statistics require continuous variables only
